options.text: Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC) of 350 cells/mm³

rationale.golden_rule: The nurse must recognize fever and chills in a chemotherapy client as a medical emergency. Priority is prompt assessment and initiation of treatment for potential neutropenic sepsis.
rationale.answer_analysis: Febrile neutropenia is a life-threatening oncologic emergency characterized by a fever (oral temperature ≥38.3°C or ≥38.0°C sustained for 1 hour) and neutropenia (Absolute Neutrophil Count [ANC] <500 cells/mm³ or ANC <1000 cells/mm³ with predicted decline to <500). Therefore, an ANC of 350 cells/mm³ and an oral temperature of 38.8°C are direct findings indicating this diagnosis. Due to the high risk of rapid infection progression and sepsis, urgent interventions are critical. Initiation of broad-spectrum antibiotics within 60 minutes of presentation is a standard, critical action for suspected febrile neutropenia. Similarly, placing the client in a private room with neutropenic precautions (also known as reverse or protective isolation) is an essential immediate action to prevent further infection, directly indicating the diagnosis and need for immediate intervention.
